text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria should avoid default on foreign debt payments to build up confidence of foreign investors, the European Union resident representative in Sofia Thomas O'Sullivan told the national radio. @

-- Private Bulgarian-Russian Investment Bank's (BRIB) shareholders authorised the board of directors to raise capital up to 25 billion levs, which would make BRIB the largest local private bank, BRIB top official said.
-- The state-owned Bulgarian Post Bank posted 12.041 billion lev pre-tax profit for 1996, bank's auditor Deloitte & Touche said.
-- The Bulgarian State Railways (BSR) is expected to raise cargo tariffs by 100 percent from April to compensate higher fuel prices, BSR officials said. @
-- The Association of Bulgarian Insurance Companies (ABIC) asked Bulgaria's prime minister Stefan Sofianski to step up measures against car thieves.
Bulgarian insurance companies are paying some $25 million a year compensations on car thefts, ABIC said.
-- Ministers from G-24 are expected to discuss in Brussels in April possible extending of financial aid for Bulgaria, European Union resident representative in Sofia Thomas O'Sullivan said. @
-- Russia's deputy prime minister Oleg Lobov arrives in Bulgaria today expected to discuss energy issues.
-- Bulgaria's monthly inflation in February is seen at 200 percent, National Statistics Institute senior official said.

-- Bulgaria's state agricultural fund Zemedelie is expected to extend 2.4 billion levs to local producers to buy for fertilisers, Agriculture minister Rumen Hristov said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
